observation: Cutting the build into ~85 small chunks (own path list, one architecture block, one verify command, one commit, red test first) after the first builder ran out: no chunk ran out of budget afterwards; stalls lost at most one uncommitted file group and were resumed with SendMessage.

First builder was handed architecture steps 1-5 in one brief, ran 95 min, wrote the module, migration and deletions but ZERO tests; the module had never executed when it reported 'done'. Its replacement wrote the seam test first and found bugs in the module and the migration immediately.

One shared git index across parallel workers: two workers' commits swept in another worker's staged files (96293faa0 carried the search_tasks filter; f5d09074e carried the tool deletion). Nothing lost, messages wrong. Rule 'commit with explicit pathspec, check git show --stat' added mid-run stopped it.

Tests asserted too loosely to fail: member-wipe test checked only toContain(owner); all four wake tests reset members so the mentioned agent was never already a member; the 'Assistant' title test hand-inserted a row shape production no longer creates; concurrency tests could not interleave on single-connection PGlite.
evidence: server review findings 1-3, re-review finding 3 and 5

observation: Three independent reviews each FAILED: round 1 UI 1 blocker + server 3 blockers; re-review 1 new blocker introduced by a fix (single fetcher narrowed server-side by block id); post-gate review 1 blocker (migration step could hit the unique direct key on a brownfield DB). Every fix wave needed its own review.
evidence: review task outputs a60eff, aafeebd, a510aef, a1b1e49

observation: Driving the real app found what tests and three reviews missed: thread page title read a field of the deleted route; mention pool ignored the host team and own agents; multi-word names unmentionable; websocket subscribe stricter than the read rule; packaged bundle dialled ws://localhost:3001.

I reported the founder gate as ready after testing only the web dev server, where no agent can run; the founder had to ask 'did you test through the desktop app'. The packaged-app run then found live updates dead. A machine-local layers/core-ui/.env (NODE_ENV=development) had been forcing dev mode into every production bundle on this machine, on main too.

Architecture left the websocket as an open amendment and then tested each end against a fake (fake hub server-side, fake client in hooks). Founder ruled nudge-and-refetch; nobody planned a real-socket test until the desktop run showed no frame ever reached the window.

Plan fixed 'adjust replaces members' and separately 'edit_task with a threadId adds the owner via adjust' without the combined case; built literally it removed everyone else from the thread. My brief to the fixing worker then asked for owner-join on later handoff, which the locked architecture forbids; the worker refused correctly.

Founder decisions taken at the gate: dial-in button removal and the unreachable session viewer accepted (viewer is a separate item); mention fixes (multi-word names, failed-wake notice) pulled INTO this item rather than deferred as I proposed; dev database may be nuked and reseeded at will.

Migrating the previous item's dev database in place was a free brownfield test (tasks got threads, old assistant thread re-hosted and found by the overlay); the demo seed loading on the new schema proved the seed sweep.

Agents stalled at the 600s output watchdog six times and were cut by a network error once; long commands had to run under nohup with a polled log. A full local gate chain (check, lint, unit, service integration, knip, deps) was run 11 times.

Local harness lane: codex exits 1 on every prompt; claude and cursor-agent adapter probes fail in harness-registry tests this branch does not touch; in the packaged app a cursor-agent request never admitted and blocked every other agent's turn (serial drain awaits admission). Thread-turn live test passes on claude, opencode and cursor-agent.
evidence: lanes h-bc3.log, h2.log; desktop run 2026-09-20; task chip task_ee5ba1f4

observation: One program-design interview, one architecture (1,800 lines) with two critique rounds, ~85 builder chunks, 3 code reviews + 1 re-review (all FAIL first), 2 web gate walks, 3 packaged desktop runs, 11 full gate chains, 2 full e2e runs, 2 harness lanes. Roughly a third of the chunks were first-pass build; the rest were test re-points for deleted routes, review fixes, gate fixes, a 30-commit comment sweep for work-item ids, and build-tooling fixes unrelated to threads. Result: 458 files, +19.9k / -30.1k lines, net about -10k.
